repo.desc: Clone URL of the repository the panel installs from. The default is this project's public repo and needs no credentials. Point it at YOUR fork if you have one — the box is editable, and a fork is the normal way to run your own copy. For a PRIVATE repository use SSH (git@github.com:owner/repo.git) with a deploy key on the node, or the install will fail asking for a password.

branch.desc: Git branch to run. Install again to update the server to the newest commit of this branch.

nodeversion.desc: Leave EMPTY to use the node's own Node.js/npm — that is what this template expects, and what requirements.binaries checks at create time. Setting a major version (e.g. 22) runs PufferPanel's nodejsdl, which downloads Node.js into the panel's binaries folder and creates node22/npm22 there. That folder is NOT on PATH on most nodes, so the alias can fail with "npm22: command not found". Only set this if your node's PATH already includes the panel binaries folder.

apikey.desc: Your rc-... Token Factory key. Passed in as the AMD_API_KEY environment variable, never written to disk, so it stays out of the console and out of git.

model.desc: Model alias served by the endpoint. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 also works.

amdurl.desc: OpenAI-compatible base URL. Change it only to point at a proxy.

host.desc: Address the bot joins. If the Minecraft server runs on this same node, use the host gateway (host.docker.internal in Docker) and the port below.

port.desc: Port the bot joins — the Minecraft server's port, not this server's panel port.

mcversion.desc: Pin a protocol version (1.21.4) or leave empty to auto-detect it from the server.

auth.desc: offline joins a private/cracked server with the fixed name ZincAI whitelisted. microsoft needs a premium account and an interactive device-code login on the first run.

scaffolding.desc: Let the bot place and remove scaffolding blocks while building.

elytra.desc: Glide across long gaps with a carried elytra and fireworks instead of walking around.

rpm.desc: Shared model-call budget. Part of it is reserved for chat so a long task can never starve replies.

mininterval.desc: Shortest gap between two action-lane calls.

heartbeat.desc: Self-prompt when nothing happens. 0 turns it off: the bot then only thinks when someone talks to it or the world changes.

reconnect.desc: After a session that spawned, retry a dropped link or a server restart with back-off under the same name. A rejected FIRST join is still fatal.

maxattempts.desc: How many times a dropped connection is retried before the process exits.

joinonstart.desc: Join the server when the process starts. Off = the process comes up idle and waits for "join" on the console.

log.desc: debug adds packet detail; warn and error quieten the console.

datadir.desc: Where memories, places, goals and metrics live. Relative to the server directory, so it is included in a normal backup.

dockerimage.desc: Only used when the server runs in Docker: the image must already contain Node.js and npm. Host, tty and standard nodes ignore this and use the node's own node/npm.

groups.description: Where the model runs and which key it uses. The key only ever exists as an environment variable.
How the bot plays and speaks. There are no modes, no alias list and no reply language: every tool is always available and the model chooses its own words.
Who may control the running bot. Console only, no prefix: pause, stop, shutdown, status, config. Nothing typed in game chat is a command.
Where the bot comes from and which runtime it uses. Host nodes use their own node/npm; Docker uses the image below.

commands: echo 'git is required: install git on the node (apt install git / dnf install git) and run Install again' && exit 1
